title: Recent challenges faced by food and drink businesses and their impact on prices
meta_description: Supply chain challenges, increasing costs and labour shortages have all played a part in increasing the UK's food and beverage prices. We look at the different issues reported by businesses within the industry and how consumers are responding.

breadcrumb.text: Recent challenges faced by food and drink businesses and their impact on prices

lede: Supply chain challenges, increasing costs, and labour shortages have all played a part in increasing the UK's food and beverage prices. We look at the different issues reported by businesses within the industry and how consumers are responding.

body.text: 4 April 2022

Food and drink have been making an increasing contribution to consumer inflation in recent months, as outlined in [our Recent drivers of UK consumer price inflation: March 2022 article](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/articles/priceseconomicanalysisquarterly/march2022). They are one reason consumers may be seeing price increases in their regular spending.
Price rises in food and drinks partly reflect challenges faced by businesses in the food and drink sector. These challenges include supply chain issues, increasing costs, and labour shortages.

Businesses were able to explain in their own words the challenges they face in free text responses to the [Business Insights and Conditions Survey (BICS)](https://www.ons.gov.uk/businessindustryandtrade/business/businessservices/bulletins/businessinsightsandimpactontheukeconomy/24march2022). We also explore other sources to show how consumers are responding to recent price rises in food and drink.

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: Businesses in the food and beverage sector have been affected by the recent rise in energy prices. In March 2022, 60% reported being affected by the rise in energy prices, compared with 38% across all sectors. A respondent to BICS explained that:

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: Prices have shot up in an unprecedented manner. Then electricity prices and wages on top of our raw materials – it's very difficult. We are struggling to keep pace with the increases. Food manufacturing business, March 2022

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: Prices have shot up in an unprecedented manner. Then electricity prices and wages on top of our raw materials – it's very difficult. We are struggling to keep pace with the increases.

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: The [Ofgem energy price cap is rising again from this month](https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/publications/price-cap-increase-ps693-april). BICS data show that 7% of food and beverage businesses reported that their fixed electricity costs were due to expire in March 2022, while 2% reported that their fixed gas prices were due to expire in March 2022.

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: More than one in eight (13%) businesses in the food and beverage sector in March 2022 reported they have variable gas prices, while 20% have variable electricity prices (compared with 15% and 19% across all businesses, respectively).

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: In March 2022, approximately 17% of businesses in the food and beverage sector reported changes to supply chains due to the end of the EU transition period, compared with 7% across all sectors.

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: We have experienced significant price increases across the supply chain. These have been anything up to and including 100% increases. Food manufacturing business, March 2022

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: We have experienced significant price increases across the supply chain. These have been anything up to and including 100% increases.

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: Meanwhile, 31% of businesses in the food and beverage sector reported global supply chain challenges in March 2022, similar to across all sectors (26%).

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: In response to challenges, BICS suggests food and beverage businesses were more likely than other sectors to have changed supply chains due to the end of the EU transition period in the first three months of 2022. Over half (55%) were using more UK suppliers, 37% were increasing diversity in suppliers, and 25% were expanding into different modes of freight (compared with 50%, 43%, and 16% across all sectors, respectively).

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: Worker shortages are reported in the food and beverage sector, but they are broadly in line with shortages across all businesses. In March 2022, 28% of businesses in the food and beverage sector reported experiencing worker shortages. This is broadly in line with that across all sectors (31%).

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: It is very difficult to recruit and maintain staff, both managerial and production staff. Food manufacturing business, March 2022

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: It is very difficult to recruit and maintain staff, both managerial and production staff.

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: In March 2022, 60% of businesses in the food and beverage sector reported a low number of applications for the roles on offer, the same as that across all businesses.

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: Labour shortages mean that we are struggling to fill vacant positions. Food manufacturing business, March 2022

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: Labour shortages mean that we are struggling to fill vacant positions.

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: Worker shortages are also reflected in higher labour costs. In February 2022, 29% of food and beverage businesses reported paying higher wages for existing employees and 30% for new employees compared with normal expectations for this time of year. This is similar to all businesses (27% and 28%, respectively).

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.text: BICS estimates show that until September 2021, the proportion of food and beverage businesses reporting price increases was broadly in line with all businesses. However, in the final three months of 2021, the proportion of food and beverage businesses citing price increases in items bought and sold increased more sharply, compared with businesses across all sectors.

body.h4: Production price rises in domestic and imported food have played a role in rising food and beverage consumer prices
body.h5: 12 -month growth rates, UK, January 2015 to February 2022, index 2015 = 100
body.text: In 2016 to 2017, when consumer food prices last rose rapidly, the main driver was a sharp increase in the cost of imported food, reflecting a weaker pound. Through most of 2021, the price of domestic food for food manufacturers increased at a faster pace than imported food, although they have now converged.

body.h3: Recent challenges in the food and beverage sector
body.h4: Production price rises in domestic and imported food have played a role in rising food and beverage consumer prices
body.h5: 12 -month growth rates, UK, January 2015 to February 2022, index 2015 = 100
body.text: With food and drink businesses paying more for both domestic and imported food, consumer prices are once again rising. Food and beverage prices for consumers have been rising since August 2021, with February 2022 seeing the highest annual growth rate (5.1%) since September 2011 (6.4%).

body.h3: Consumer spending patterns have changed as prices rise because of business challenges
body.text: Consumer spending patterns have changed as prices rise because of business challenges

body.h3: Consumer spending patterns have changed as prices rise because of business challenges
body.text: The Opinion and Lifestyle Survey (OPN) asked adults about changes in their cost of living over the last month. In March 2022, 87% of respondents reported that their cost of living had increased (a rise from 62% when this question was first asked in November 2021). Of those adults who said their cost of living had increased, 31% reported spending less on food shopping and essentials.

body.h3: Consumer spending patterns have changed as prices rise because of business challenges
body.text: Between December 2021 and February 2022, around a third of businesses in the food and beverage sector reported turnover decreased compared with normal expectations for this time of year. In comparison, around a quarter of businesses across all sectors reported turnover decreased compared with normal expectations for this time of year.

body.h3: About the data
body.text: About the data

body.h3: About the data
body.text: The indicators and analysis presented in this article are primarily based on responses from the Business Insights and Conditions Survey (BICS), of businesses with 10 or more employees.

body.h3: About the data
body.text: BICS is a voluntary, fortnightly survey that captures businesses' responses on how their financial performance, workforce, prices, trade, and business resilience have been affected, over a two-week reference period. A detailed description of the weighting methodology can be found in our recently published [Quality and Methodology information report](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/economicoutputandproductivity/output/methodologies/businessinsightsandconditionssurveybicsqmi).

body.h3: About the data
body.text: BICS responses were sifted by their Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) Code. These were:

body.h3: About the data
body.text: SIC 10 – Manufacture of food products

body.h3: About the data
body.text: SIC 11 – Manufacture of beverages

body.h3: About the data
body.text: SIC 46.17 – Agents involved in the sale of food, beverages and tobacco

body.h3: About the data
body.text: SIC 46.21 – Wholesale of grain, unmanufactured tobacco, seeds and animal feeds

body.h3: About the data

body.h3: About the data
body.text: SIC 47.2 – Retail sale of food, beverages and tobacco in specialised stores (excluding SIC 47.26: Retail sale of tobacco products in specialised stores)

body.h3: About the data
body.text: The quotes used in the article are derived from the free text responses within BICS. They reflect the overall experiences reported by businesses between 7 March to 20 March 2022. Some have been summarised and all safeguard the anonymity of the respondents.
